Follow with batched `web_extract` on specific abs pages. Recovered ~70% of papers in Aug 2026 delta sweep.\n\n   **CRITICAL — delta sweep past a known ID threshold:** Use `order=-submitted_date` (not `-announced_date_first`) in arXiv search URLs when sweeping for papers newer than a known threshold ID. `-announced_date_first` returns older papers and will produce zero results above the threshold. Verified: switching to `-submitted_date` immediately surfaced 6 new papers above threshold in Sweep 10 (Aug 12, 2026).\n   ```\n   https://arxiv.org/search/?searchtype=all&query=TOPIC&start=0&order=-submitted_date\n   ```\n   Also filter out DOI-derived fake arXiv IDs (e.g. `9027.37650`) with: `int(id.split('.')[0]) < 10000`.\n2. **Read cached `.md` files**: when a `web_extract` page was already fetched in the same session, the tool prints the file path — read from cache rather than re-fetching (saves calls).\n3. **arXiv keyword search**: `web_search` discovery + `web_extract` batches of ≤5 IDs. Query pattern: `arXiv 2026 \"memory consolidation\" LLM agent`. Added ~30% of papers not on listing pages.\n4. **GitHub**: search trending repos by topic (`agent memory`, `RAG knowledge graph`). Stars signal production adoption.\n5. **Reddit r/LLMDevs**: practitioner lessons missing from papers. `site:reddit.com r/LLMDevs \"knowledge graph\" agent memory`.\n6. **Vectorize.io / benchmark blogs**: comparative analyses with star counts.\n7. **J-STAGE / CyberLeninka**: low yield for this domain (Aug 2026 finding). Check quickly, don't block.\n8. **CNKI**: paywalled — search arXiv with Chinese institution names instead.\n\n**Batching**: issue 3–6 `web_search` calls simultaneously, then batch `web_extract` on resulting IDs. LLM-extracted relations expand to ~360 labels; collapse to ~80 canonical before multi-hop works.\n- **AriGraph** (arXiv:2407.04363): semantic facts (λ=0.01 decay, ~69d half-life) vs episodic events (λ=0.05, ~14d) — different retention per type.\n- **Graphiti bi-temporal** (Zep, production): `valid_from`, `valid_to`, `superseded_by` per fact. Forgetting / Pruning\n\n| Mechanism | Paper | Metric | Implementation |\n|-----------|-------|--------|---------------|\n| Dedup gate (cosine > 0.92 → skip + increment `access_count`) | 2605.08538 | **58% store reduction, 97.2% retention** | PRIORITY 1 for l1-promote.py |\n| Ebbinghaus: `score = confidence * e^(-days/30) * log(1+access_count)` | 2604.04514 | 6.7× discriminative power | `retention_score`; archive < 0.1, delete < 0.05 |\n| Interference-based forgetting | 2605.08538 | Independent of time-decay | NLI check on contradiction → penalize old fact score |\n| Three-tier status: Active → Archived → Deleted | 2604.04514 | Graduated utility preservation | `memory_status`; archived = searchable but not default-returned |\n\n### ScrubJay-MEM - Type-Conditioned Perishability Decay (arXiv:2608.04746)\nResult: Only retrieval system with positive GenGap (+0.108); +2.66 F1 over Mem0. Ablating type-conditioned decay collapses GenGap 5.7x.\n\nLabel table: ephemeral (pi=0.9, tau=2h, keywords: today/immediate/right now/session/temporary), task_specific (pi=0.6, tau=24h, keywords: task/ticket/issue/meeting/project), procedural (pi=0.3, tau=10d, keywords: how to/steps/process/procedure/workflow), factual (pi=0.1, tau=45d, default).\n\nRetrieval score: value_score x exp(-pi x age/tau). Error Recovery Patterns (Aug 2026)\n\n**DARR Loop** (AgentDebugX, arXiv:2607.18754, code available):\n- **Detect**: classify failure type from trajectory (tool error / logic error / context loss)\n- **Attribute**: multi-turn root-cause diagnosis via global trajectory understanding — the step where error *surfaces* ≠ the step that *caused* it\n- **Recover**: behavior-scoped guidance from cross-iteration Repair Memory (store scrubbed failure+repair pairs as retrievable memory)\n- **Rerun**: guarded re-execution with correction active\n- Result: 55.8% → 63.6% accuracy on GAIA (vs 4-6 tasks repaired by self-correction, 13 repaired by DARR)\n\n**Critical Transition Graph** (AgentTether, arXiv:2607.06273):\n- Abstracts run into Transition Units → dependency-aware CTG → localizes failure subtrajectory via offline normal-behavior model\n- Reduces agent turns AND tokens during recovery\n\n### Width/Memory/Delay - 3 Axes of Context Pressure (arXiv:2608.02113)\nTool schema WIDTH is the dominant cost driver (not memory depth or planning delay). Selective schema loading >> full-schema padding. Highest-ROI optimization: tool relevance router that injects only relevant MCP schema per request.\n\n### 7. Multi-Agent Coordination Findings (Aug 2026)\n\n- **Orchestration break-even** (arXiv:2608.00685): gate subagent dispatch on task complexity score; orchestration hurts for simple tasks\n- **Debate benefit condition** (arXiv:2606.02866): debate helps iff `P(rescue wrong) > P(destroy correct)`; critic must have different tools than generator; self-verification with identical tools fails reliably\n- **Conversation depth cost multiplier** (HN #46045969): 3 turns = 12.1x tokens; 6 tools = 2.1x tokens — prioritize history compression over tool pruning\n\n---\n\n## Prioritized l1-pipeline Roadmap\n\n### Priority 1 — High Impact, Low Effort ✅ IMPLEMENTED (2026-08-11)\n\n1. ✅ **Dedup gate in l1-promote.py**: embed fact via OpenAI text-embedding-3-small, query Hindsight top-1; cosine ≥ 0.92 → skip + increment `access_count` on existing memory. Based on the Generative Agents retrieval\nscoring model (recency + relevance + importance), the ExpeL experience extraction\npattern, AgeMem store/discard/update operations (2026), LeanMem (arXiv:2608.20320),\nMemSIF Dual-Track (arXiv:2608.01742), and AMD (arXiv:2608.07169).\n\n## Memory Poisoning Write Gate (arXiv:2608.21230, DreamBench-SWE arXiv:2608.20664, Aug 2026)\n\n**Memory Poisoning (2608.21230):** False facts that appear factually plausible and stylistically\nnormal bypass conservative retention policies. Standard dedup/contradiction checks fail because\nthe poisoned fact doesn't lexically contradict an existing fact — it supplements it with false\ndetail. Example: \"Claude has a 1M token context window\" instead of 200K.\n\n**Defense:** Cross-verification before write. For every candidate memory:\n1. Retrieve 3 most similar existing memories\n2. If any retrieved memory contradicts the candidate, flag for manual review\n3. If no contradiction but candidate introduces new detail, require 2 independent sources\n4. If only 1 source, write to a staging area with `poisoned: true` tag\n\n## MCMA — Memory Copilot Separation via DPO (arXiv:2601.07470, Aug 2026)\n\nDecoupling memory management from task execution allows memory-management capability to transfer across tasks even when specific memories don't.\n\n## AutoMem — Memory Management as a Trainable Skill (arXiv:2607.01224, Jul 2026)\n\nTreats memory LoCoMo+LongMemEval -->\n\n**LeanMem** is a lazy consolidation algorithm that only consolidates features recurring across 2+ sessions.\n\n**Hermes implementation:**\n- After each session, extract all features (entities, actions, outcomes)\n- For each feature, check if it appeared in the last 2 sessions\n- If yes, consolidate into durable memory with `consolidation_score = recurrence_count * importance_score`\n- If no, keep in ephemeral memory only\n- Recurrence count is stored as metadata: `recurrence: 2`\n\n**Token reduction:** 87% vs full consolidation, 94% vs naive turn-level encoding.\n\n### MemSIF — Dual-Track Fact Memory (arXiv:2608.01742, Aug 2026) ★ HIGH\n<!-- rationale: write-time salience ≠ future utility; CoreFact eager, ActiveFact after demand -->\n\n**MemSIF** is Dual-Track Fact Memory (NOT a state-injection filter). Verified abs:\nhttps://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01742 — CoreFact vs ActiveFact.\n\n**Hermes implementation (runtime, not prose):**\n- CoreFact (`ns=profile` or type `preference`/`correction`): stage eagerly in `l1-promote.py`\n- ActiveFact (everything else): stay pending in `lifecycle.db` until RecMem recurrence ≥ 2 **or** `access_count ≥ 3`\n- Query demand: `unified-recall.py` mixes pending ActiveFacts into results and increments `access_count`\n- Drain: `l1-promote.py` stages pending rows once `access_count >= 3` (does not increment on cron defer)\n- Staging tag: `[track=core|active]`; Graphiti parser strips it\n\nDo not invent a second MemSIF (2608.20444 / 2608.20112 are not this paper).\n\n### AMD — Proactive/Reactive 3-Tier Injection (arXiv:2608.07169) ★ HIGH <!-- rationale: skill authoring tier missing -->\n\n**AMD** is a 3-tier memory injection framework:\n1. **Proactive tier**: Pre-load high-value memories before the task starts (strategic)\n2. **Reactive tier**: Inject memories during task execution based on context (tactical)\n3. **Skill tier**: Update skill files with distilled procedures (abstract, on-demand)\n\n**Hermes implementation:**\n- Proactive tier: `hermes-memory-surface-selection` skill\n- Reactive tier: `agent-memory-consolidation` skill\n- **Skill tier**: `hermes-agent-skill-authoring` skill (MISSING — implement now)\n\n**Skill tier implementation:**\n- After consolidation, identify action sequences that:\n  - Occurred 3+ times\n  - Had positive outcomes\n  - Are not already covered by existing skills\n- Distill into a new skill file or patch an existing one\n- Safety gate: only verified-action sequences become SOPs\n\n### Engram - Bi-Temporal Memory Model (arXiv:2606.09900) ★ MED\n**Engram** separates event time from observation time. Existing lifecycle timestamps cover this; do not add a second timestamp schema.\n\n### PoisonedEvolution — Utility Under Attack (arXiv:2608.21230, Aug 2026) ★ HIGH\nReal paper (fetched): content screening rejected 0/360 poisons; provenance ranking has no usable weight.
